fullPassage:
Logan's Speech

"The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you admire. It could be a historical figure, a celebrity, or even someone you personally know in your life," Ms. Harper told the class. My classmates began brainstorming a list of people they might pick — mostly athletes, singers, and actors. However, I knew right away who my speech was going to be about. Grandma is the person I admire the most. Writing a speech about her would be a piece of cake.

A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to deliver a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms sweat. I'm too shy to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer. How on earth can I speak in front of everyone? I couldn't sleep at all that night.

The big day for the speech finally arrived, and I felt more anxious than ever. I had spent the previous week imagining how my classmates would react to my speech. I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think. I wasn't putting much thought into what I was actually going to say. I figured I could just speak off the top of my head. After all, I was going to talk about my grandmother. I didn't need any notes.

I was sweating as I walked up to the front of the class. My heart was racing so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face turning red. I didn't know where to look. I blanked out. I just stood there silently.

Ms. Harper tried to help me out. "Start by telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan." I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. Then Ms. Harper said, "How about telling us a bit about why you admire her so much?" I barely managed to share a short story about her. After that, I just rushed to my seat and put my head in my hands. I knew I had messed up. I hadn't said all the things I wanted to say.

The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to talk about the speech. I said, "I'm embarrassed about the speech. I must have looked like a fool. I know I could have done better."

"It's quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice. "What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?"

"I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn't good enough."

She replied, "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech." That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn't have been able to make my classmates like what I wanted to say. I really should have focused on my performance.

A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.

I felt nervous again when the big day finally arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I walked up to the front of the class and looked out into the audience. My heart began to race, and I took a deep breath to calm it down. While my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to get my whole message across. When I was done, I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!

The Golden Rule of Listening

Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?

Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.

Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.

det.analysis:

❌ ② admire — broadcasting — slice
✅ ③ admire — brainstorming — piece ←정답

(A) admire(존경하다)가 문맥에 적합. acquire(획득하다)는 부적합.
(B) brainstorming(아이디어를 짜내다)이 적합. broadcasting(방송하다)은 부적합.

det.tip: a piece of cake = 아주 쉬운 일. brainstorm = 아이디어를 짜내다.

After that, I just <u>rushed</u> to my seat and put my head in my hands. I knew I had messed up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 rushed와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 그 후 자리로 서둘러 돌아가 머리를 손에 묻었다. 발표를 망쳤다는 것을 알았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① hurried(서둘렀다): rushed의 동의어.
❌ ② dashed(돌진했다): rushed와 유사한 의미.
❌ ③ sprinted(전력 질주했다): rushed보다 더 빠른 의미, 반의어 아님.
✅ ④ lingered(꾸물거렸다) ←정답: rushed(서둘렀다)의 반의어.
det.tip: rush = 서두르다. linger = 꾸물거리다, 오래 머물다.

questions.passage:
"

She replied, "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be <u>focusing</u> on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech. " That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn't have been able to make my classmates like what I wanted to say.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 focusing과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 네가 통제할 수 있는 한 가지에 집중해야 한다 — 발표를 어떻게 하는가.
det.analysis:
❌ ① concentrating(집중하는): focusing의 동의어.
❌ ② examining(조사하는): 집중과는 다르지만 반의어는 아님.
✅ ③ neglecting(무시하는) ←정답: focusing(집중하는)의 반의어.
❌ ④ emphasizing(강조하는): focusing과 유사한 방향.
det.tip: focus = 집중하다. neglect = 소홀히 하다, 무시하다.

questions.passage:
(A) After the long hike, she sat down and noticed her heart started to <u>race</u> wildly.
(B) He decided to enter the <u>race</u> next month and began training every day.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 race가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (A) After the long hike, she sat down and noticed her heart started to race wildly. (B) He decided to enter the race next month and began training every day.

det.korean: (A) 긴 하이킹 후 앉았는데 심장이 빠르게 뛰기 시작했다. (B) 다음 달 경주에 참가하기로 결심하고 매일 훈련하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 경쟁하다 — (B) 인종
❌ ② (A) 빠르게 뛰다 — (B) 인종
❌ ③ (A) 경쟁하다 — (B) 경주
✅ ④ (A) 빠르게 뛰다 — (B) 경주 ←정답
(A) heart race = 심장이 빠르게 뛰다 (본문에서도 My heart began to race 사용).
(B) enter the race = 경주에 참가하다.
det.tip: race (동사) = (심장이) 빠르게 뛰다. race (명사) = 경주, 경기.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"to practice a play, speech, or piece of music in preparation for a public performance"

det.korean: 공연을 위해 연극, 발표, 음악을 연습하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① perform(공연하다): 실제 공연 행위, 연습이 아님.
✅ ② rehearse(리허설하다) ←정답: 공연 전 연습이라는 정의에 정확히 부합.
❌ ③ compose(작곡하다/작문하다): 만드는 행위이지 연습 아님.
❌ ④ memorize(암기하다): 암기와 리허설은 다름.
det.tip: rehearse = 리허설하다, 예행연습하다. 본문: I rehearsed how I would stand...

questions.passage: This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of __________ (stand) in front of the entire class made my palms sweat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 반 전체 앞에 서는 것을 생각하니 손에 땀이 났다.
det.analysis: The thought of __________ (stand): 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사 형태 필요. stand → standing.
det.tip: 전치사(of) + 동명사(-ing) 구조. The thought of standing = 서는 것에 대한 생각.

questions.passage: I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which __________ (contain) key phrases about important facts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 매일 거울 앞에 서서 말하고 싶은 것을 복습했다. 중요한 사실에 대한 핵심 구절이 담긴 큐 카드를 사용했다.
det.analysis: which __________ (contain): 관계대명사 which 뒤, 과거 시제 맥락. contain → contained.
det.tip: 과거 시제 문맥(stood, went, used)에서 which절도 과거 시제 사용. contain → contained.

questions.passage:
Good listeners can help speakers by creating __________. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. 

Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 경청자는 화자를 도와 ____을(를) 만들 수 있다. 경청자로서 주의 깊게 듣고, 건설적이고 도움이 되어야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a competitive speaking atmosphere(경쟁적 발표 분위기): 건설적·도움이 되는 맥락과 불일치.
❌ ② a strict evaluation standard(엄격한 평가 기준): 도움이 되라는 맥락과 모순.
❌ ③ a dramatic performance style(극적 공연 스타일): 경청과 무관.
✅ ④ a positive communication climate(긍정적 의사소통 분위기) ←정답: 좋은 경청의 결과.
det.tip: climate = 분위기, 풍토. positive communication climate = 긍정적 의사소통 분위기.

questions.passage: A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to __________ like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 몇 주 후 또 다른 발표 과제가 주어졌다. 처음처럼 ____하고 싶지 않았다. 이번에는 발표를 연습했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① raise the bar(기준을 높이다): 실수의 맥락과 무관.
✅ ② drop the ball(실수하다) ←정답: 첫 번째 발표를 망친 것을 가리킴.
❌ ③ break the ice(어색한 분위기를 깨다): 발표 실수와 무관.
❌ ④ steal the show(주목을 독차지하다): 망친 상황과 불일치.
det.tip: drop the ball = 실수하다, 잘못하다. like the first time = 처음처럼.
